section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that fulfilling God's will requires creating the will within the framework of "place" (the order of Hishtalshelus), which is a novel act achieved specifically through the service of "with all your might."
section.t: The explanation is,
that the meaning of "they do the will of the Place" is that one must make
(one must create)
the will in the Place.
For "Place" refers to the order of Hishtalshelus,
and Ein Sof Himself is above the aspect of place,
as it is brought in the Midrash24
on the verse25
"Behold, a place is with Me,"
He is the place of the world, but the world is not His place,
therefore one must make the will in the Place,
that is,
not only is the will in the aspect of Place a novelty,
but the matter of the will itself is a novelty,
for Ein Sof is not at all from any of these attributes26,
for He is above all the Sefiros and also above the aspect of will that is within them,
and in order for there to be will, this is a novelty,
as it is said, "May it be [His] will,"
meaning that the aspect of will should be renewed.
And in order for there to be the aspect of will, this is through the fulfillment of Torah and Mitzvos,
as per the statement27
"It is pleasing before Me that I said and My will was done,"
that by causing pleasure before Him, blessed be He, through the fulfillment of Torah and Mitzvos,
then "My will is done,"
meaning the aspect of will is renewed.
And all this is the renewal of will in general,
which is accomplished through the fulfillment of Torah and Mitzvos in general.
However, in order to do the will of the Place,
that is, to renew the will in the Place,
the fulfillment of Torah and Mitzvos alone is insufficient,
rather, this requires the love of "with all your might,"
for in order to make the will in general,
the service as it is from the aspect of "with all your heart and with all your soul" is also sufficient,
but in order to renew the will in the Place,
this specifically requires the service as it is from the aspect of "with all your might."
And this is that the second portion of the Shema is the aspect of "they do not do the will of the Place,"
because the service of "with all your might" is lacking in it,
and specifically through the service of "with all your might" does one do the will of the Place.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that there are two levels of will—lower will (born from intellect) and higher will (above intellect)—and this is illustrated in the animal soul and then understood in the divine soul.
section.t: The explanation is,
that behold, in will there are two levels,
lower will and higher will.
And these two aspects of will exist in the animal soul,
and from this it will also be understood in the divine soul,
and likewise it will be understood above.
For behold,
the lower will in the animal soul is like one who desires business,
for this will is born from intellect,
for when he understands how the matter of business is good for him,
then he desires it,
and from the will he thinks about the business,
speaks and acts regarding it,
and this will is the lower will,
since it is born from intellect.
And the higher will is a will that is above intellect,
like one who desires to live,
who desires his own existence,
for this will is not from intellect or reason.
And from this aspect of will that desires to live,
the will that desires business is also found,
that is, the will that desires to live is depicted through the intellect into particular wills according to the modes of intellect that he has understood what is good for him,
for all the particular wills are the will that desires to live as it has been depicted through the intellect.
And behold,
the difference between lower will and higher will is,
that lower will is limited,
for since it is born from intellect,
it is limited according to the limitation of the intellect.
And also, this will is only in the externality of the soul,
for being that it is only from contemplation,
it reaches only that place in the soul that the intellect reaches,
but not so the higher will, which is above intellect, is without limit,
and it is the will that is from the inwardness of the soul.
And from this it will also be understood in the divine soul,
that there is in it a lower will and a higher will,
for the lower will is what one desires in Divinity from contemplation,
and the higher will is the aspect of "to love Havayah your God, for He is your life"28,
which is not from reason,
but rather this is his life-force.
Like
(in the animal soul)
the will that desires to live.
And it is the aspect of the higher will, the ratzon that is the source of all wills29.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "doing the will of the Place" means drawing down the higher, unlimited will into the limited order of Hishtalshelus, which is accomplished through the unlimited service of "with all your might" in the soul.
section.t: And likewise it will be understood above,
that the lower will is the will as it comes into Hishtalshelus through Chochmah,
and the higher will is the will that is above reason,
from which all wills are drawn
(and as above in the animal soul, that all wills are drawn from the will that desires to live),
the ratzon that is the source of all wills.
And this is the matter of "they do the will of the Place,"
that is, the making of the will that is above Hishtalshelus,
the higher will,
in the Place,
in Hishtalshelus,
for by drawing down the will that is above Hishtalshelus into Hishtalshelus,
then below there will be conduct that is without limit,
for even within the limitation of Hishtalshelus, the unlimited will shine.
And therefore, at the time that one does the will of the Place, then "strangers will stand and shepherd your flocks,"
for even below there will be conduct without limit.
And it is like the statement30
"On that day Havayah will be One,"
for now it is not as I am written, I am read31,
meaning that now Havayah is in concealment,
but not so in the future, Havayah will be revealed below.
And this drawing down is through the love of "with all your might"24,
for in order to reach the aspect of the unlimited that is above, this is through service with the unlimited that is in the soul,
for although this is not true unlimited,
for it is only "your might"32,
nevertheless, since in man it is at least without limit,
and it is the higher will in man,
behold through this he also draws down the higher will that is above,
and this is the matter of "they do the will of the Place."
